records.issue_text: [BUG] `assignment_source.to_dict()` returns a `datetime` in the dict passed to `sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async`, causing `EncodeError: Object of type datetime is not JSON serializable` with the standard JSON serializer, so any assignment with a source never enqueues its outbound task, silently disabling cross-system propagation on the inbound path
records.rationale: `AssignmentSource.to_dict()` returns `asdict(self)` for a dataclass that includes `queued: datetime = timezone.now()`, so the resulting dict includes a raw `datetime` object. That dict is passed directly into Celery `apply_async` kwargs as `assignment_source_dict` in `sync_group_assignee_outbound` (`assignment_source.to_dict() if assignment_source else None`). If the task queue uses a JSON serializer (common default), a `datetime` in kwargs will raise a serialization/EncodeError and prevent enqueuing.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] `from_dict` performs no type validation, so a string `integration_id` (e.g., from JSON) constructs a 'valid' `AssignmentSource` where the same-integration cycle check compares str to int, evaluates `False`, and bypasses cycle prevention
records.rationale: In `AssignmentSource.from_dict`, the code does `return cls(**input_dict)` with no runtime type validation/coercion. Since dataclasses don’t enforce annotations, `integration_id` can become a `str` if the incoming dict has a string (e.g. JSON-derived data). The cycle-prevention check in `IssueSyncIntegration.should_sync` compares `sync_source.integration_id` to `self.org_integration.integration_id` using `==`; a `str` vs `int` comparison will be `False` and thus won’t block same-integration sync cycles as intended.

records.issue_text: [BUG] `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` default is evaluated once at class-definition/import time, so every AssignmentSource constructed without explicit `queued` shares the same frozen timestamp (import time), making the field semantically dead for stale/replay detection; the `test_to_dict` assertion passes while the value is wrong
records.rationale: In `src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py`, the dataclass defines `queued: datetime = timezone.now()`. That default expression is evaluated once at class definition/import time, so every `AssignmentSource(...)` created without an explicit `queued` will share the same timestamp. This makes `queued` incorrect for per-event timing/staleness semantics, and the `test_to_dict` only checks non-None so it would not catch this.
